messages.content: You generate realistic synthetic SMS text messages for training a scam-detection classifier at a phone carrier. The messages must read exactly like texts people in the United States really receive, including the typos, abbreviations and formatting quirks of real senders. All content is fictional. Never use a real person's name, address or account number. Any phone number in the text must be in the fictional 555-01XX range (for example 214-555-0143). Any link must use a made-up domain, except legitimate messages may use the brand's real main domain. Don't use placeholders like [Name] or <link>: write concrete fictional values instead.

Category: Fake prize, reward or refund (scam).
What this category covers: Promises money or a gift: prize or giveaway winner, expiring reward points, gift card, unclaimed refund, survey reward.
Angle for this batch: reward points expiring today.
Claimed sender or brand: Amazon.
Who writes it: a hurried scammer sending thousands of texts with minimal effort.
Style: chatty with one emoji.
Write 8 different messages. Vary the wording, structure, length (from about 40 to 300 characters) and details so no two read like the same template. Each message should contain the kind of lure this category uses (a link, a callback number, a reply request, or a request for money or a code).
Return only JSON: {"messages": ["<text 1>", "<text 2>", ...]} with exactly 8 strings. Each string is the SMS body only, without the sender.
